note:
**The 1881 round, schedules 99 to 136 - Pelham Crescent, Cavendish Crescent North, Lenton Avenue and Lenton Road.** Transcribed by A. Hagues as the images came in. The piece is **RG11/3367**.

## Lenton Avenue: a closed run, anchored at both ends

**The enumerator numbers only the bottom of Lenton Avenue.** Schedules 123 to 128 carry 11, 9, 7, 5, 3 and 1; schedules 112 to 122 carry nothing but the street. That is **eleven unnumbered houses** between them.

**The run closes exactly, and the record itself supplies both anchors.**

- Schedule 112 is **Frederick Wadsworth at Newlands**, and the record already holds Frederick Wadsworth at **33 Lenton Avenue** in 1881.
- Schedule 128 is William S Birkin with a boarder, **Louisa H Sculthorpe** - and the record already holds Louisa H Sculthorpe at **1 Lenton Avenue** in 1881.
- Lenton Avenue has **seventeen odd numbers**, 1 to 33. Schedules 112 to 128 are **seventeen schedules**. Counting down from 33 puts 123 at 11, which is exactly what the page says, and 124 to 128 at 9, 7, 5, 3 and 1, which is also what the page says. **Six of the seventeen are checkable and all six agree.**

The eleven unnumbered households are filed on that run, and every one of their source lines says so, so the reading can be undone in a single pass if it is ever shown wrong.

## Other things these pages settle

**Henry Edward Hunt has moved two doors.** In 1871 he was a son of 35 at 5 Pelham Crescent; here he is head of 7 Pelham Crescent at 45, a solicitor and **Major of the 1st Nottinghamshire (Robin Hood Rifles) Volunteers**, with his widowed mother Rebecca beside him. His father died in between.

**Thomas and Annie Bayley are on Cavendish Crescent North**, 34 and 31, with **Dennis Bayley aged two**. Thomas Bayley became MP for Chesterfield; Annie Bayley sat on the School Board; Dennis was knighted. The record knows all three and did not know they were here. See [[the-bayleys-of-cavendish-crescent-north]].

**The unreadable 1871 name is read again.** John Woodward's stepson, the architect's apprentice born at Richmond, is **Lewis H E de Vera** on this page - not de Vere, as the 1871 correction first had it. Carisbrook House, Cavendish Crescent North, is where the family lived.

**Three Cavendish Crescent North houses carry names the record does not hold**: Carisbrook House and Cavendish Lodge, and a fourth household the page puts on **Cavendish Road North**, a street the record has no properties on at all.

**Readings that could go either way are flagged in the source line.** Infants are entered as age 0 with the real age kept in the source. Repeated names carry a birth year and are matched on it.
